title: An orphaned change is attributed and resolved, never left in the tree
intention: Every uncommitted change in either repo that no open ticket's build claims is ATTRIBUTED FIRST. One the transcripts or the artifact journal attribute to cc or the builder is committed into its ticket or moved to the trash. One that cannot be attributed is surfaced to Akien as an inbox question naming the paths, and never removed. Nothing lies silent in the tree. (8v (open-c08119a71e1a, 2026-10-07): Akien edits the active repo rarely but really ('it's happened twice since we started in february', fewer than six handed to us to commit).)
traces_to: Law 5 (the repo is itself the state of the machine, and an orphan is state no record explains). Law 7 (an error stays loud: an orphan is named until resolved). Akien's 8u answer, 2026-10-07.
how: (a) bin/cmd/orphans, a python script in the bin/cmd style, with subcommands list (the default), adopt and remove. (b) The roots come from env CAIRN_ORPHANS_ROOTS (colon-separated, a fixture seam), defaulting to the two repos. The transcripts dir comes from CAIRN_ORPHANS_TRANSCRIPTS, defaulting to ~/.claude/projects. The trash goes through bin/cmd/trash with its own env seam. (c) The claimed set is the union of chain_for_ticket(t)['decompose'] sub_problems writes_to over open tickets, repo-relative, read with berths_root from CAIRN_ORPHANS_BERTHS for the fixture. (d) Attribution scans the transcripts newest-mtime-first and stops at the first tool_use naming the absolute path. (e) The proof is at the path above, six teeth, PROVES keyed on this ticket, and it builds its repos with git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t in a tempdir. ATTRIBUTE FIRST (8v): a path is attributed only by a transcript tool call naming it or a journal entry for it; mtime alone attributes nothing. `adopt` and `remove` refuse an unattributed path. `cairn orphans` opens ONE question for the unattributed set, `cairn question open --ticket 7bb99eed0629 "Are these uncommitted paths yours: <paths>?"`, and it opens it only when no open question of this ticket already names the same set.
falsifier: Done when bin/proofs/test_orphans_are_attributed_and_resolved.py is green under bin/cairn test --netns. (1) In fixture repos, an open fixture ticket whose decompose claims a.py, with a.py and b.py both dirty: `orphans` lists b.py only. (2) A fixture transcript whose Write call names b.py attributes b.py to that session and timestamp. (3) `adopt b.py --ticket <id>` leaves b.py clean and HEAD's message names the id. (4) `remove` on an untracked c.py leaves it in the fixture trash and absent from the tree; on a modified tracked d.py it leaves a .patch in the trash and d.py at HEAD. (5) adopt of a claimed path, or under an unknown ticket id, refuses and writes nothing. Red at HEAD: no bin/cmd/orphans. (6) A dirty path that no fixture transcript or journal names lists as unattributed: `remove` and `adopt` refuse it and leave it in the tree, and `orphans` opens one question bound to 7bb99eed0629 naming it. A second `orphans` run opens no second question.
why: Akien, 8u, 2026-10-07: 'there is only you and the builder. so it was one of you two... not the first time you've had orphaned changes. a fixit ticket to resolve those is in order if no other remedy presents itself.' 316b's lane will refuse crossings on unclaimed dirt; this is the way through it. Measured instance: 3fef5a02da2d's lab rows, left uncommitted by cc. 8v (open-c08119a71e1a, 2026-10-07): Akien edits the active repo rarely but really ('it's happened twice since we started in february', fewer than six handed to us to commit), so the fixit attributes first and never removes what it cannot attribute.
